newsitem.title: INDIA: India says ready for talks with Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: India says ready for talks with Pakistan.

text.p: India on Monday congratulated Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on taking office and said it was willing to resume peace talks on a wide range of issues including disputed Kashmir.

"I wish you success in the heavy tasks that lie ahead," Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said in a letter to Sharif, who was sworn in on Monday. "We are ready and willing to have wide-ranging comprehensive talks on all issues of mutual concern."

Earlier on Monday after winning a confidence vote in Pakistan's National Assembly, Sharif said he wanted to revive long-stalled peace talks with India, but said New Delhi must be willing to let Kashmiris decide their own future.

India and Pakistan have fought three wars since independence in 1947, two of them sparked by tension over Kashmir. India, which controls two thirds of the Himalayan region, says Kashmir is an integral part of its territory.
"You might construe that the prime minister (Deve Gowda) is suggesting that Kashmir could be one of the issues to discuss with Pakistan," a Foreign Ministry official said.

Deve Gowda said in his letter, released in New Delhi, that India believed cooperation between the longtime foes would benefit the people of both nations. "To this end, we seek an early resumption of dialogue between our two countries, at appropriate level," he said.
